run.data-root: <scratch>/dr (user scope, server :65363 bound via --port 0). Never ~/.ai-raccoon; 7721 answered 401 before and after and was never bound. All scratch processes stopped after the run.
run.note: 1.49.1 is not on nuget.org yet (latest published 1.48.0), so the global tool was force-updated from a local Release pack. Items added beyond the template, carried from the 1.44.0 run or for changes since: memory-engine-unconfigured-warning, absolute-relevance-floor-keeps-exact-matches (the floor is now granite's 0.79, ADR-0108), full-recall-ranking-order, bundled-engine-on-gpu (ADR-0108), watch-ingests-new-file-types (1.49.0), categorized-exit-codes (ADR-0107, replaces the 1.44.0 attach-flag-removed and f39-no-mint-guard items). Not re-run this time: attach-or-start-identity-proof, f49-secret-layout, busy-bank-refusal-and-best-effort-bump (no changes to their code paths since 1.44.0 by commit subjects; not re-verified).

findings-against-prior-runs.prior-claim: full-recall-ranking-order: fail, fixed on main by 1.44.2 ('leader outranks neighbour boost', #666).
findings-against-prior-runs.what-is-actually-true: The 1.44.2 fix covers a leader that both legs rank first. A leader ranked fts 1 / vector 7 (identifier buried in a long note) still loses to two vector-only chunks of one file under the default sourceLambda 0.1 and consolidationThreshold 0.1: it ranks third. Setting either to 0 restores it to first.
findings-against-prior-runs.so-what: The defect is narrower than it was, but not gone. The default floor hides it, so only minRelativeScore 0 callers see it.

findings-against-prior-runs.prior-claim: absolute-relevance-floor-keeps-exact-matches: probed with 'AIR-4471' against a short note.
findings-against-prior-runs.what-is-actually-true: Under granite (1.47.0+) a short note that contains the identifier scores cosine 0.85 against the bare identifier, above the 0.79 floor, so that probe passes whether or not keyword hits are exempt. It no longer tests the exemption. A long note with the identifier buried in it (cosine 0.770) does.
findings-against-prior-runs.evidence: 'AIR-4471' cosine 0.854, 'QZX7K2P' 0.838 (both above the floor); 'vk83jq' 0.770 (below the floor, kept by fts).
findings-against-prior-runs.so-what: The floor probe needs a content cosine below the engine's floor. Check the evidence cosine before accepting it.

findings-against-prior-runs.prior-claim: build-and-install-global-package: a local `dotnet pack` is the build under test.
findings-against-prior-runs.what-is-actually-true: Since ADR-0108 a fresh worktree's `dotnet pack` exits 0 and produces a package without model_fp16.onnx_data (the ~97 MB weights file is fetched by scripts/download-embedding-model.py, which CI runs before packing). Installing that package would ship a tool whose bundled engine cannot load. scripts/verify-tool-package.py catches it; the pack step does not.
findings-against-prior-runs.evidence: First pack: ai-raccoon.osx-arm64.1.49.1.nupkg 31.9 MB, no onnx_data entry. verify-tool-package.py: 'FAIL: Models/granite-embedding-small-english-r2/model_fp16.onnx_data missing'. After download-embedding-model.py: 180.5 MB, onnx_data present, verifier OK.
findings-against-prior-runs.so-what: The build step must run download-embedding-model.py and verify-tool-package.py before installing. Nothing in the pack fails when the weights are missing.

RID package 180.5 MB against published 1.48.0's 180.4 MB (onnx_data ships twice in it, at Models/ and tools/.../Models/).
items.observed-result: The installed tool is this commit's build, byte-identical. The pack only includes the bundled model when it was downloaded first; see findings-against-prior-runs. Side effect: the update removed the 1.48.0 store directory the owner's running :7721 server loaded from, and that server's code search now refuses with 'code-engine-unloadable ... Restart the MCP server'. The refusal names the cause and the fix.
items.acceptance-reason: Version and binary match the tree. The pack gap is recorded as a finding, not a failure of this build.

items.expected-result: ADR-0107: removed flag -> 11 Usage.Unparseable; settings verb on a data root with no bank -> 31 Bank.NoBank and creates nothing; --port 0 on a dialling verb -> 13 Usage.UndialablePort; --transport stdio -> 14 Usage.RemovedTransport

items.evidence: root --attach exit=11 'Unrecognized command or argument '--attach'.'; serve --attach exit=11. no-bank exit=31 'ai-raccoon: no bank exists at '<dr-typo>/memory.db' — create it with ... serve, or check --data-root for a typo'; ls: No such file or directory. port0 exit=13 'cannot dial --port 0: expected 1-65535 ...'. '--transport stdio serve' exit=14; '--transport https' exit=14. 'serve --transport stdio' exit=11, printing 'Hint: --transport stdio was removed; ...'.

items.acceptance-reason: All documented cases match. The post-verb --transport case is a misplaced token by the grammar (11), which ADR-0107 allows; the hint wording is cosmetic.
